report.source_text: The patient ultimately was admitted to the intensive care unit for further evaluation and management for what was likely pulmonary barotrauma secondary to the repetitive dives. The patient was successfully extubated the following day. Subcutaneous emphysema continued to be present but was improving. The patient was evaluated by pulmonology in the hospital who recommended outpatient evaluation to include pulmonary function tests and instruction to not go diving anymore.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 19-year-old male presented with voice change, facial and neck swelling, chest pain, and shortness of breath after diving in a river. Physical exam revealed neck and shoulder swelling with palpable crepitus and oropharyngeal edema with muffled voice. Chest radiograph showed large volume mediastinal and neck emphysema with severe subcutaneous emphysema. Chest CT revealed fluid filling bilateral lower lobe bronchi and diffuse interstitial emphysema, consistent with pulmonary barotrauma. Neck CT confirmed extensive emphysema without airway injury. The patient was admitted to ICU, intubated, then successfully extubated with improving subcutaneous emphysema and was advised against further diving. Pulmonology recommended outpatient pulmonary function testing.
